analysis:
All three changed files are documentation or changelog only: two new changelog.d/*.md entries and edits to docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (lines 3 and 54-59 on head). No source code is in this batch, so no executable behavior, authorization, encryption, attestation or billing path changed.

The changelog entries describe provider behavior that is not visible here. Nemotron Super now serves json_object/json_schema response formats alongside tools, and the media request body bound rises from 8 MiB to 40 MiB. The docs update the worst-case media charge figures: 4.67 GiB per image, 4.54 GiB per video, 25.6 GiB for 16 images.

The 40 MiB bound increases the memory the provider may be asked to hold for one request. This touches the availability concern around TB-007 and TB-003 (T-016-style resource pressure, T-050 media plaintext handling). The docs say the media charge is quoted against the memory ledger before admission. The source implementing that quote (NemotronSuperServingPolicy.mediaChargeBytes, the ingress body-bound check) is not supplied. I cannot confirm that the larger bound is enforced before decode or that the charge covers it, so I record that as an unverified contract rather than a finding.

The JSON-format-with-tools change likewise has no code to check. The documented behavior is fail-closed: an answer without calls that is not valid JSON returns 422, and a required or named tool_choice still needs its call. No T-008-style plaintext fallback is implied.

Remaining question for later passes: if the code changes land in other batches, check that the 40 MiB bound is enforced prior to base64 decode and that temp-file handling for inline video (T-050) is unchanged. Also check that coordinator-side body limits match the provider bound.
